Chapter 08120 BPMPROCESSING

Crows

Every evening the crows go home from work.

Crows spend the day inspecting roofs, windows, wires and streets, then commute east in the evening. Their observations reach the Morning Meeting, but a view is not the whole truth. They return to uncertain places and change position when a familiar perch stops telling them enough. To a passerby, this looks like birds waiting around. Some days that is exactly what careful work looks like.

A crow returns to the dark upstairs music window. A strip of faded party ribbon caught on blackberry thorns appears to confirm that the gathering has gone. It carries a loose end to a lower perch, then notices the same fabric tied to a chair beside an open downstairs door. Traffic masks the sound whenever it faces the old window. From the new angle, music arrives and the host carries another chair inside. The ribbon was real; the conclusion was wrong. The bird leaves with a corrected observation. Beneath the bramble, the same short pulse repeats, still missing what the crow has now seen.

The ruleNever ask a crow what department it works for.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
